Sofia is designing a park that is made up of a rectangle and two semicircles, as shown in the diagram. The area of the park must be $16\,{km}^{2}.$ What should be the radius $r$ if Sofia wants a park with the smallest possible perimeter? Do not round the answer.

$r=$
{{field-1}}
$\text{km}$
question.worked_solution:
We let $r$ be the radius of the circular sector (the same for both semicircles) and let $x$ be the other side of the rectangle. Then, we want to minimize the perimeter

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =2x+\pi r+\pi r \\  & =2x+2\pi r.\end{aligned}
$$

We know that the area is fixed at $16\text{ km},$ so we also have the constraint condition

$$
16=2rx+\pi {r}^{2}.
$$

Now, by making $2x$ the subject of the constraint equation and taking into account that $r>0,$ we find that

$$
\begin{aligned}16 & =2rx+\pi {r}^{2} \\ 2rx & =16-\pi {r}^{2} \\ 2x & =\frac{16}{r}-\pi r.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging this into our expression for $P,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}P & =\frac{16}{r}-\pi r+2\pi r \\  & =\frac{16}{r}+\pi r.\end{aligned}
$$

We want to minimize $P,$ so we need to differentiate $P$ and set the derivative equal to zero. Computing the derivative gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}^{′}(r) & =-\frac{16}{{r}^{2}}+\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the derivative equal to zero and solving for $r$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{16}{{r}^{2}}+\pi  & =0 \\ \pi  & =\frac{16}{{r}^{2}} \\ {r}^{2} & =\frac{16}{\pi } \\ r & =\sqrt{\frac{16}{\pi }} \\ r & =\frac{4}{\sqrt{\pi }}\,\text{km}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we confirm that $\frac{4}{\sqrt{\pi }}$ is a minimum using the second derivative test.

Since the second derivative ${P}^{″}(r)=\frac{32}{{r}^{3}}>0,$ the stationary point $r=\frac{4}{\sqrt{\pi }}\,\text{km}$ is a minimum.
